y-m-78-13.title: Finishers lost 3.2 kg on average: is that the effect of the challenge?
y-m-78-13.topic: Survivorship bias and rewriting an ad phrase
y-m-78-13.goal: Know that data that leaves out people who dropped out can inflate the effect, make an example yourself where the average of finishers can differ greatly from the overall average, and rewrite the ad phrase so readers are not misled.
y-m-78-13.material: An exercise app is advertising with the phrase 'Average weight loss of 30-day challenge finishers is 3.2 kg!' The app's challenge is joined voluntarily by those who start it, and the records of people who quit partway are not kept in the app.
y-m-78-13.thinking.0: Sorting out the information needed to judge the effect
y-m-78-13.thinking.1: Making an example where the overall average is smaller than the average of a part
y-m-78-13.thinking.2: Rewriting into a sentence that reduces readers' misunderstanding
y-m-78-13.prereq.0: This task is at the 'H2' difficulty (one step beyond H1) in this platform's production allocation, and it does not mean that the Ministry of Education assigns this subject to a particular grade. Assume you already know the prerequisite concepts below.
y-m-78-13.prereq.1: How to think about the overall average from group averages and numbers of people
y-m-78-13.prereq.2: The idea that how a sample was gathered affects the conclusion
y-m-78-13.s.s1.prompt: To judge the effect of the challenge from this phrase alone, what more information is needed? Choose everything that is needed.
y-m-78-13.s.s1.hint.0: First write down which people alone the number in the phrase is the average of.
y-m-78-13.s.s1.hint.1: Think about who is left out, and whether their results would have raised or lowered the average.
y-m-78-13.s.s1.o.a: The number of people who started and the proportion of them who finished.
y-m-78-13.s.s1.r.a: Depending on what percent of those who started are finishers, the same average has a different meaning.
y-m-78-13.s.s1.o.b: The total number of app downloads and the number of people who saw the ad.
y-m-78-13.s.s1.r.b: The number of downloads is not directly related to the challenge results.
y-m-78-13.s.s1.o.c: The weight changes recorded by the people who quit partway.
y-m-78-13.s.s1.r.c: If those who quit are left out, it becomes an average of only the people with good results.
y-m-78-13.s.s1.o.d: The age of the ad model, the place the ad was filmed, and the date it was filmed.
y-m-78-13.s.s1.r.d: The age of the ad model and the filming location are not related to the effect of the challenge.
y-m-78-13.s.s1.o.e: The weight changes of similar people who did not take part.
y-m-78-13.s.s1.r.e: Without something to compare with, you can't know whether the 3.2 kg is because of the challenge.
y-m-78-13.s.s1.explain: You need the proportion of those who started who finished, the results of those who quit, and a comparison with people who did not do the challenge. The number of app downloads or the model's age is not related to the effect.
y-m-78-13.s.s2.prompt:
Suppose 200 people started, the finishers (f people) lost 3.2 kg on average, and the dropouts (200−f people) lost g kg on average (negative means weight gain). Enter 2 different (f, g) for which the average loss of all 200 who started is 1 kg or less.
① f is an integer from 10 to 190
② g is from −1 to 1
③ Overall average (3.2×f+g×(200−f))÷200 ≤ 1
y-m-78-13.s.s2.hint.0: Check with a few numbers how the overall average moves if you take the number of finishers to be small.
y-m-78-13.s.s2.hint.1: Change the dropouts' average g, calculate the left side of condition ③, and compare it with 1.
y-m-78-13.s.s2.ok.c1: f is an integer from 10 to 190.
y-m-78-13.s.s2.fail.c1: The number of finishers f must be an integer from 10 to 190.
y-m-78-13.s.s2.fail.c2: The dropouts' average loss g must be from −1 to 1.
y-m-78-13.s.s2.ok.c3: The overall average is 1 kg or less.
y-m-78-13.s.s2.fail.c3: The overall average is greater than 1 kg.
y-m-78-13.s.s2.explain: For example, if 50 of 200 are finishers and the average of the 150 dropouts is 0.2 kg, the overall average is (160+30)÷200=0.95 kg. The finishers-only average of 3.2 kg is correct, but looking at everyone who started, it can be much smaller.
y-m-78-13.s.s3.prompt: Rewrite this phrase so readers are not misled, and add the reason for the change in one sentence. (Example: 'The average of 30-day challenge finishers ...')
y-m-78-13.s.s3.hint.0: Write down what fact the reader comes to believe after reading the phrase.
y-m-78-13.s.s3.hint.1: Think about how to put into the phrase the part where that belief can differ from the facts.
y-m-78-13.s.s3.placeholder: Example: Of the people who started the 30-day challenge, ...
y-m-78-13.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Did you put 'what percent of those who started finished' in the revised phrase?
y-m-78-13.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Did you make clear that it is the average of finishers only, so it won't be read as the overall effect?
y-m-78-13.s.s3.selfAssess.2: Is the revised sentence readable as an ad and free of falsehood?
y-m-78-13.s.s3.model.0: Of the people who started the 30-day challenge, 25% finished, and the finishers' average weight loss is 3.2 kg. The results of those who quit partway are not included.
y-m-78-13.s.s3.model.1: The finishers' average weight loss is 3.2 kg, but this is the result of only those who went to the end. The average of everyone who started may be smaller than this, so the finishing rate is given together so it isn't read as the overall effect.
y-m-78-13.s.s3.modelNote.1: This answer also writes the reason for the change.
